Math. Phys. 259 (2005), 257--286]. Second, we prove that the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) is at least 3/2.

papers.title: Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: Given an edge-colored graph, the wild number measures how close the graph is to having a spanning tree in every color. We investigate this parameter for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, with particular emphasis on minimum proper colorings and equitable $2$-colorings. For complete graphs, we determine the full range of wild numbers attainable by equitable $2$-colorings and show that, although every value in this range occurs, the expected wild number of a uniformly random equitable $2$-coloring tends to $0$ as the order of the graph grows. For minimum proper colorings of $K_n$, we establish a general lower bound, determine the exact wild number for $3 \le n \le 12$, and conjecture that the lower bound is sharp for all $n$. We also develop structural conditions on ideal wild sets and use them to obtain upper bounds and analyze the performance of a natural greedy algorithm. For complete bipartite graphs, we prove a sharp upper bound for equitable $2$-colorings and determine the wild number exactly for minimum proper colorings. Finally, we apply these results to Cartesian products of complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, obtaining lower bounds for the wild number under minimum proper and product colorings.

papers.title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
papers.abstract: The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falcón-Cortés, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $ξ_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $ξ>ξ_0$ anywhere else. We prove that, for all $ξ_0\in (0,1)$, if $ξ$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $ξ= ξ_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses"). Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour Pólya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued Pólya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

papers.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
papers.abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.

papers.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
papers.abstract: Consider the bipartite Erdős--Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $γ= n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Marčenko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $γ$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.

papers.title: Ordinary lines, point degrees, and matroid density
papers.abstract: For every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with full affine span, we prove that some point lies on at least $n+1-2n/(d+1)$ spanned lines, which is best possible in every dimension. By successive contraction, this implies the sharp bound $r+(\ell-3)\binom r2$ on the number of elements of a simple rank-$r$ complex-representable matroid excluding $U_{2,\ell}$ as a minor, which removes the sufficiently-large-rank assumption from the bound of Geelen, Nelson, and Walsh. An arithmetic application shows that rank-$r$ integer matrices whose maximal minors have absolute value at most $Δ$ have at most $O(Δr^2)$ distinct columns, resolving a question of Averkov and Schymura. We prove that a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^3$ determines at least $n^2/40$ ordinary lines whenever no plane contains more than $2n/3$ of the points. This answers a question of Basit, Dvir, Saraf, and Wolf. We also prove upper bounds on average line length and lower bounds on the number of points incident to many spanned lines in high-dimensional point sets. The proofs combine contraction of concentrated flats with normalization of the point vectors and second- and fourth-moment estimates on their pairwise correlations. This approach builds on the design matrix method.

papers.title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.

papers.title: Unavoidable flats in GF(q)-representable matroids
papers.abstract: We show that, for any finite field $\mathbb{F}$ and positive integer $k$, a simple $\mathbb{F}$-representable matroid $M$ with sufficiently high rank contains a rank-$k$ flat which is either independent in $M$, or is a projective or affine geometry over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}$. This generalizes a result for matroids representable over prime fields due to the first two authors. As a corollary, we obtain a Ramsey theorem for matroids representable over a finite field $\mathbb{F}$. For an integer $k$, in any $2$-colouring of the points of an $\mathbb{F}$-representable matroid of sufficiently high rank, there is a monochromatic rank-$k$ flat.

papers.title: Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes
papers.abstract: We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.

papers.title: $λ$-geodesic convexity of the squared sliced-Wasserstein distance
papers.abstract: The squared Wasserstein distance with respect to a fixed target measure is not a convex function along Wasserstein geodesics over $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $d\geq 2$. Still, in dimension $d=1$, this function is $2$-geodesically convex. We prove that the square of the sliced-Wasserstein distance (which is a distance constructed averaging one-dimensional Wasserstein distances) is $λ$-geodesically convex (possibly with $λ\leq 0$) on sets of measures satisfying upper bounds on their density, when the target measure satisfies some given geometric conditions. We also present some consequences of this result in the study of the sliced-Wasserstein flow.

papers.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

papers.title: Uncovering higher-order interactions from memory in observed dynamics
papers.abstract: Many complex systems involve group interactions, which can readily be represented by higher-order structures such as hypergraphs. However, when observing a system's dynamical evolution, establishing whether that evolution actually results from higher-order interactions, or whether pairwise interactions suffice to explain the data, remains a challenge. Even in the simple case of a temporal sequence of nodes visited during a diffusion process, such a task is intricate. Indeed, group interactions leave their traces as memory on the observed nodes, while path dependence in a purely pairwise process can mimic that same footprint without any group structure. To resolve this, we propose an inference pipeline based on a hidden Markov model (HMM) that tests, directly from an observed sequence of nodes carrying no group labels, whether higher-order interactions are required to describe the dynamics. The HMM latent states represent higher-order interactions, seen as hyperedges of an unobserved hypergraph, so that their detection becomes a model selection problem between the HMM class and a class of null models without higher-order interactions. We first validate this approach on synthetic node sequences generated from random walks on graphs and hypergraphs, showing that it recovers both the number and the composition of the underlying hyperedges, while correctly rejecting them when the generating process is pairwise. As a second step, we consider a validation based on empirical data, namely empirical trajectories of ball possession in football matches. This application shows that the pipeline goes beyond providing statistical evidence of the presence of higher-order interactions, and yields interpretable underlying structures: the recovered hyperedges map directly onto recognizable tactical team formations.

papers.title: An Analytic 0.48-Approximation for Non-Monotone k-Submodular Maximization under a Matroid Constraint
papers.abstract: We give a randomized polynomial-time $0.48$-approximation for maximizing a nonnegative non-monotone $k$-submodular function under a matroid constraint, for every $k\ge2$. The algorithm combines a top-two label rule with a nested-chain potential and maximum-weight matroid bases. Its analysis reduces the approximation guarantee to a one-dimensional time allocation: a uniform local lower bound leads to a linear differential equation, concavity closes the remaining interval, and two elementary budgets complete the proof. A strict saving in the time budget absorbs sampling and discretization errors, yielding the exact $0.48$ guarantee in the value-oracle model.

papers.title: The parity module of a matroid
papers.abstract: We introduce the parity module of a matroid with coefficients in a field $\mathbb{k}$. When $\mathbb{k}$ has characteristic zero, we show that the parity module of a matroid is isomorphic to its intersection cohomology module, yielding a new intrinsic characterization of the latter. The structure and dimension of the parity module can vary depending on the characteristic, giving rise to characteristic-dependent generalizations of the Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials of matroids. When the matroid is realizable over the complex numbers, the parity module is isomorphic to the hypercohomology of the parity sheaf supported on the arrangement Schubert variety of any such realization. We also introduce the notion of pure modules over any field $\mathbb{k}$ and show that they satisfy a matroid analogue of the Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne-Gabber decomposition theorem: Every pure module over the graded Möbius algebra decomposes as a direct sum of shifts of the parity modules of matroids obtained by restricting to flats.

papers.title: Gaussian approximation for the integrated intensity of counting processes: application to Hawkes processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish quantitative central limit theorems for the integrated fluctuations of the intensity of a counting process. Building on the work of Coutin and using the Clark-Ocone formula, we first derive a general upper bound on the Wasserstein distance between a Gaussian random variable and the normalized integral of the centered intensity. We then apply this result to subcritical linear Hawkes processes. In this setting, we prove that the integrated fluctuations of the intensity converge in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable, with a convergence rate governed by the tail behavior of the resolvent associated with the underlying Volterra equation.

papers.title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $α$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract: Score-based generative models driven by $α$-stable L{é}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $α$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails. At any positive generation time, stable dynamics produces power-law tails with index $α$, whereas Brownian dynamics remains light-tailed. For a target with tail index $ν$, asymptotically correct extreme-quantile scaling is possible precisely when $α$=$ν$. These results identify tail-index matching as a principled mechanism behind the ability of stable generative models to capture extreme events.

papers.title: The quasi-convex Rockafellar theorem
papers.abstract: Rockafellar showed that every cyclically monotone operator is contained in the subdifferential of a convex function, and characterized the maximal ones. We establish the quasi-convex analogue of this theorem, with no assumption on the operator: in any separable Banach space, a setting we show to be sharp, every cyclically quasi-monotone operator is contained in the normal cone operator of a quasi-convex function. In finite dimension, we characterize maximal cyclically quasi-monotone operators and show that they are maximal quasi-monotone. Unlike in the convex case, the potential is not unique, and we build it from a preference relation obtained through successive preorders. As applications, we extend Afriat's theorem on revealed preferences in economics to infinite data sets, and obtain Kantorovich-type potentials for a supremal optimal transport problem.

papers.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent: A Nonlinear Time Series Perspective
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the statistical behavior of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with constant step size under the framework of iterated random functions. Compared to previous studies establishing the convergence of SGD in probability measure, e.g., Wasserstein distance, our approach directly provides the convergence in Euclidean distance by showing the Geometric Moment Contraction (GMC) of SGD. This new convergence can address the non-stationarity of SGD due to fixed initial points and can provide a more refined asymptotic analysis of SGD. Specifically, we prove quenched central limit theorem, invariance principle and $α$-stable convergence for averaged SGD (ASGD) regardless of initialization. Furthermore, we provide a novel perspective to understand the impact of step sizes in SGD by studying its derivative with respect to the step size. The existence of stationary solutions for the derivative processes is shown, enabling the use of interpolation to recover the full-trajectory of SGD. Subsequently, we utilize multiple step sizes and show an enhanced Richardson-Romberg extrapolation with improved bias representation, which brings ASGD estimates closer to the global optimum. Finally, we propose a new online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for the extrapolated ASGD. Empirical confidence intervals are constructed and the coverage probabilities approach the nominal level as $n$ grows.

papers.title: $q_x$-Bass Martingales: Optimality, Existence and Convergence
papers.abstract: We introduce the class of $q_x$-Bass martingales, extending the notion of $q$-Bass martingales. These are martingale couplings with prescribed marginals whose transition kernels are closest to a given family of reference kernels $(q_x)_{x \in \mathbb R^d}$ in the sense of a suitable weak optimal transport problem. We show that $q_x$-Bass martingales are optimizers of this problem and establish a strong duality result. Building on this duality, we introduce an algorithm for their computation and, under compactness assumptions on the prescribed marginals, prove its convergence, thereby establishing existence. We then specialize to one-dimensional marginals and show that the algorithm reduces to a fixed-point iteration.

papers.title: Heat Kernel Estimates for Random Walks with Killing on Transient Graphs
papers.abstract: We give matching two-sided estimates for heat kernels obtained from Schrödinger operators $Δ+W$ on weighted graphs. The graphs we consider are transient and admit two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates for the Laplacian $Δ$, and the potentials $W$ decay to zero at infinity. We offer two proofs for one of our main results: one using the Feynman-Kac formula, and one without using it. Our results apply to fractal-type graphs such as graphical Sierpinski carpets, among other examples.

papers.title: The forward-loop-erased ants walk
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a new variant of the ants walk: a model of reinforced random walks for the phenomenon of a colony of ants being able to find the shortest path between their nest and a source of food. In this model, the nest and the source of food are two distinguished nodes in a finite graph. The ants perform successive random walks on this graph, started at the nest and stopped when they first hit the food source; the transition probabilities of each random walk depends on the trajectories of the previous ants, through some edge-weights that represent the amount pheromones deposited on each edge. In our new variant of the model, the ant (1) forgets loops made on the way to the food as soon as they are made, and (2) comes back to the nest following this loop-erased version of its forward trajectory, and deposits pheromone on the edges it crosses by doing so (i.e. adds one to these edges' weights). We say that the ants "find the shortest path" if, almost surely as the number of ants tends to infinity, the proportion of ants that travel along a graph-geodesic path from the nest to the food tends to one and the proportion of ants that travel along the remaining edges tends to zero. We are able to prove that this new variant of the model finds the shortest path when the graph distance between the nest and the source is at most 2. The strength of our result is that there is no other assumption on the shape of the graph. We prove this result using stochastic approximation theory, the electrical network method for random walks on weighted graphs, and the theory of weighted uniform spanning trees (WUSTs). In particular, the link with WUSTs is unique to the model studied in this paper due to the way the ant erases loops on the outward journey.

papers.title: Fully Dynamic Random-Walk Quantities on Undirected Expanders and $κ$-Uniform Directed Graphs
papers.abstract: We study fully dynamic data structures for random-walk quantities on undirected expanders and fast-mixing directed graphs. For an unweighted graph whose normalized Laplacian has spectral gap at least $γ$, we give a $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ effective-resistance data structure with expected update time $O(γ^{-4}\varepsilon^{-2}\log n\log^4(n/\varepsilon))$ and expected $O(1)$ query time. For directed graphs, somewhat surprisingly, the OMv conjecture precludes a fast data structure based on rapid mixing conditions alone. To address this, we introduce the notion of $κ$-uniform directed graphs, which requires the stationary distribution to $κ$-approximate the uniform distribution, and show that in this setting, random walk based data structures with $\text{poly}(κ, \log{n}, \varepsilon^{-1})$ update/query times are possible.

papers.title: Matroid-Aware Spectral Certificates for Multiplicative Coverage Approximation
papers.abstract: We maximize the weight of edges covered by selected vertices, together with nonnegative individual rewards, under an arbitrary matroid constraint. The continuous coverage objective is quadratic and need not be concave. Our method searches projections onto a small set of directions and solves a concave subproblem for each projection center. A coverage-specific inequality converts the subproblem bounds into a multiplicative guarantee, while matroid rounding restores an integral solution. Let $A$ be the weighted adjacency matrix and $D$ the diagonal matrix of singleton values, restricted to positive-value elements after objective-preserving preprocessing. Set $\varrho=λ_{\max}(D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2})$. For an integer budget $q\ge0$, let $τ_q$ be the smallest nonnegative threshold for which $A+τ_qD$ has at most $q$ negative eigenvalues on the span of differences of matroid bases. We obtain the factor $1-\varrhoτ_q/[2(\varrho+τ_q)]-\varepsilon$ in time $(2+q/\varepsilon)^{O(q+1)}N^{O(1)}$, where $N$ is the binary input length and a zero-over-zero loss is zero. The algorithm returns a rational upper bound on the integral optimum. A separate exact-algebraic construction produces polynomial-bit low-rank rational corrections with positive threshold slack; its proof isolates eigenvalues, keeps eigenspace bases unnormalized, and approximates scalar factors only at the final step. The numerical proposal prototype is not used to justify this complexity statement. Supplied certificates also yield robustness to locally bounded edge additions. These are threshold-dependent coverage guarantees, not a new general spectral-search principle or a universal approximation improvement.

papers.title: Optimal transportation under McKean-Vlasov dynamics
papers.abstract: We study a broad class of stochastic transport problems under controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics, allowing control of both drift and volatility, with weak terminal constraints. In contrast to the classical Schrödinger problem, the reference dynamics depend on the evolving law of the process, leading to nonlinear optimization problems on path space, while the terminal constraint is formulated through weak optimal transport, permitting a flexible treatment of distributional targets. This framework encompasses several problems of current interest, including the mean field Schrödinger problem, martingale optimal transport, and Schrödinger-Bass bridges. We establish three main results. First, we prove the existence of optimal controls under general coercivity, continuity, and convexity assumptions. Second, we derive a convex dual representation that extends weak Kantorovich duality and stochastic optimal transport duality to controlled McKean-Vlasov dynamics. Finally, for the mean field Schrödinger problem, we prove convergence, at the level of value functions, of the associated finite-particle Schrödinger bridge problems to the mean field limit, thereby identifying the nonlinear problem as the exact infinite-particle limit of finite-particle Schrödinger bridges. As a byproduct, we establish the existence of an optimal mean field Schrödinger potential, providing a variational foundation for duality in nonlinear stochastic transport.

papers.title: Quantifying research uniqueness with Unbalanced Optimal Transport: Case studies of ten leading universities in neuroscience
papers.abstract: Research evaluation has developed around quantity, citation impact and, more recently, the accumulation of research excellence, but these dimensions remain largely dependent on citations, which describe how research is received rather than what it contains. We propose uniqueness as a complementary dimension and measure it with the Research Uniqueness Index (RUI), which asks how far a university's research sits from what is typical in its field, using no citations but the content of the research itself. Each researcher is represented by an embedding of their abstracts, and an unbalanced version of Optimal Transport returns the share of that work which cannot be matched into a random sample of same-field researchers, the standard population; that unmatched share is the score. Because every researcher is scored, a university is a distribution rather than one number, and we treat that distribution as the indicator: it shows whether uniqueness is spread across an institution or concentrated in a few groups. Quantiles summarise it and, being quantiles, do not reward size. Since uniqueness is defined only relative to a field, we demonstrate the index within one, neuroscience (Scopus, 2021-2025; 9,861 reference researchers). All ten universities studied sit well above the standard (RUI_median 0.40-0.53 versus 0.27) and five specialised institutes higher still (0.57-0.73), the most unique work often confined to a narrow niche that the same scores name. RUI is uncorrelated with citation impact, and a controlled test confirms that it tracks displacement from the field rather than topical concentration; results are robust to an alternative embedding and replicate in computer science and economics. The index is not intended as a league table: the gap above the standard and the researcher-level niche structure are stable, whereas the order among adjacent universities is not.

papers.title: Optimal Transport for Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection
papers.abstract: The continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem is investigated in this paper through a rigorous integration of backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and Kantorovich duality theory. We propose a novel analytical framework for addressing feedback control in McKean-Vlasov stochastic systems. By solving three coupled systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), we derive an explicit, closed-loop optimal feedback investment strategy.

papers.title: Spectral radius and edge-disjoint spanning trees of graphs with edge connectivity
papers.abstract: Let $τ(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees contained in a graph $G$. Zhang and Fan [J. Graph Theory, 2026] posed the problem of determining the corresponding tight spectral-radius condition for every $s$-edge-connected graph with \[ k+1\leq s\leq2k-1, \] together with a characterization of the associated extremal graphs. In this paper, we completely resolve this problem.

papers.title: Covariance-Rank Rounding and a Sharp Integrality Gap for a Matroid Edge-Coverage Moment Lift
papers.abstract: Selecting vertices covers their incident edges, but a matroid can prevent selecting the combinations that cover the most weight. We study whether pair-selection information improves rounding from a semidefinite relaxation of this problem. A feasible point $(x,Y)$ records individual and paired selection values. Its relaxation objective is $U$, and the matrix $Y-xx^\top$ has rank $d$. We compare the feasible marginal vectors obtained by fixing one element as selected or excluded, then round only the best vector. For $d\ge1$, the resulting basis has value at least $(3/4+1/(4d))U$. The procedure is deterministic and polynomial-time for a supplied exact rational point and an independence oracle. Weighting the covariance spectrum by the objective gives a stronger version of the bound. To show the rank factor is sharp, we construct a rank-$2m$ rational linear matroid and $m$ disjoint four-cycles with integral optimum $3m+1$, relaxation optimum $4m$, and an optimal covariance matrix of rank $m$. Thus the relaxation has limiting reciprocal integrality gap $4/3$, despite its conditional constraints. One valid pair-exclusion inequality makes it exact on this family, as an explicit semidefinite certificate shows. The result concerns rounding and the strength of this relaxation; it does not supply a low-rank optimal point or a fixed universal approximation improvement.

papers.title: A Matroid Generalization of Weighted Popular Matching: Characterization and Algorithm
papers.abstract: We study a problem that unifies two major generalizations of popular matchings in the one-sided preference model. In a bipartite graph in which each vertex, or applicant, on one side has preferences over the adjacent vertices, a matching is called popular if it does not lose a head-to-head election against any other matching. Since the seminal work of Abraham, Irving, Kavitha, and Mehlhorn, who gave the first polynomial-time algorithm for finding a popular matching, numerous generalizations of the popular matching problem have been investigated. Two prominent directions are weighted popular matchings, in which each applicant is assigned a voting weight, and popularity problems under matroid constraints. The former admits a polynomial-time algorithm due to Mestre, while the most general form of the latter is the popular common independent set problem, for which a polynomial-time algorithm is given by Kavitha, Makino, Schlotter, and Yokoi. In this paper, we introduce the weighted popular common independent set problem, which simultaneously generalizes weighted popular matchings and popular common independent sets. Our main result is the first polynomial-time algorithm for this problem. A key ingredient of the algorithm is a solution-independent characterization of weighted popular common independent sets, which we establish in this paper. As consequences of our algorithmic result, we obtain polynomial-time algorithms for several previously unresolved problems, including weighted popular matchings with matroid constraints and weighted popular branchings.

papers.title: Optimal scaling and curvature correction for constrained MCMC on spheres
papers.abstract: Sampling Gaussian measures restricted to nonlinear manifolds in high dimensions requires a proposal kernel that respects both geometric constraints and dimensional scaling requirements. We introduce tangent preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN), which combines a manifold projection with a cancellation of the ambient Gaussian contribution, leaving only a geometric residual. Considering a shifted sphere with $\sqrt d$ scaling of radius and centre as a tractable benchmark embedded manifold, we prove that uncorrected tangent pCN results in a proposal noise scale of order $d^{-1/6}$ (compared to $d^{-1/2}$ for a tangent random-walk). We establish asymptotic optimal tuning for the geodesic expected squared jump distance which is maximised at an acceptance probability of 0.574 for the family of drift-corrected tangent proposals containing tangent pCN and tangent MALA. We also prove a joint diffusion limit for the parallel and orthogonal coordinates to the sphere's centre vector of tangent pCN. The orthogonal diffusion speed matches the limiting geodesic expected squared jump distance and is maximised at acceptance probability 0.574, whereas the parallel speed is maximised at 0.712, demonstrating that optimal tuning depends on the observable. We then identify an intrinsic precision correction characterised by potential Hessian and Ricci curvature that yields a proposal kernel with dimension-independent fixed step size limit. We discuss a generalisation to arbitrary hypersurfaces and present nondegenerate scaling of tangent pCN applied to conditioned diffusions under resolution refinement.

papers.title: On Over-Conservatism Under Low-Probability Extreme Events: A KL-Regularized Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Planning Method
papers.abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy makes power systems more vulnerable to low-probability extreme events, elevating system planning to a critical role in ensuring reliability. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) based on the Wasserstein distance is widely used to address this challenge. However, we find that the conventional Wasserstein ambiguity set tends to excessively amplify the probabilities of low-probability extreme events, leading to over-conservative investment decisions. To mitigate this over-conservatism, this paper proposes a novel ambiguity set that modifies the Wasserstein distance with a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence regularization term. By leveraging the KL divergence's sensitivity to relative probability changes, the proposed set effectively curbs the unrealistic magnification of low-probability events. A two-stage distributionally robust planning model built upon this new ambiguity set is developed to optimize the installed capacity of photovoltaic, wind, and energy storage. The complex model is then reformulated as an equivalent exponential cone program with strict theoretical proofs, making it computationally tractable. Numerical results on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems reveal the over-conservatism of standard Wasserstein DRO under low-probability extreme events and validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed planning model and solution algorithm.

papers.title: Local-discrepancy ambiguity sets for distributionally robust optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of data-driven ambiguity sets for distributionally robust optimization (DRO) that aim to enhance the local inference accuracy of an unknown distribution. Building on optimal transport-based discrepancy measures, we depart from the conventional paradigm of monolithic ambiguity balls, which rely on a single global transport budget to capture distributional uncertainty. Instead, we introduce local-discrepancy ambiguity sets, where the support of the distribution is partitioned into predefined regions and transport cost constraints are imposed locally to each region. This added flexibility allows for a more refined characterization of plausible distributions by preventing highly imbalanced transport across regions. As a result, the proposed approach can yield less conservative and more robust decisions, particularly in settings where decisions depend on the local properties of the sample space. We further derive tractable reformulations of the resulting DRO problems and demonstrate through simulations that our method can outperform traditional Wasserstein ambiguity sets in terms of decision quality.

papers.title: A Generalized Elephant Random Walk with Time-Dependent Memory
papers.abstract: The elephant random walk (ERW) is a discrete-time random walk with complete memory. At every step the walker chooses one of the previous increments at random and then either repeats with a constant probability $p\in [0,1]$ or reverses it. Since its introduction by Schütz and Trimper, the model has become a useful probabilistic framework for studying long-range dependence, anomalous diffusion, reinforcement, and phase transitions. This paper proposes a generalized ERW model with time-dependent memory. In this generalized model, the usual constant memory parameter $p$ in the standard ERW is allowed to change with time. The cental limit theorems, and the law of the iterated logarithm and some other strong laws are obtained.

papers.title: Entropy, isoperimetry and the total variation profile of random walks
papers.abstract: The total variation profile $\mathrm{TV}_n$ of a random walk measures how far its distribution at time $n$ is from being invariant under the generators. Three lower bounds are given: an elementary bound $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$ in terms of the speed $L(n)$; a bound by the entropy increment $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$, which is a reverse Pinsker inequality; and a bound in terms of the entropy and the isoperimetric profile. Deciding whether the entropy-increment bound always improves on the isoperimetric one is related to conjectures on the growth of the entropy and of groups. The motivation comes from the question of whether the distributions of a random walk can be transported back onto their translates at bounded cost.

papers.title: Very high genus double Hurwitz numbers via mixing times
papers.abstract: We obtain very high genus asymptotics for double Hurwitz numbers when both the size $n$ and the genus $g$ go to infinity, under the constraint that $g$ grows much faster than $n$, more precisely that $\frac{2g}{n}-\ln n\to\infty$. Our proof relies on adapting arguments about the mixing time of the transposition random walk introduced by Diaconis and Shahshahani.

papers.title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
papers.abstract: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids. We also explain how the DLSF relates to the computation of currents in an electrical network in the presence of a gauge field. The partition function of the DLSF is shown to be the determinant of the twisted Laplacian, for which we also give a matrix-tree type theorem that computes its characteristic polynomial. We initiate the study of the twisted Laplacian determinant as a functional on the space of connections, and give a first order expansion of it in a neighborhood of the trivial connection, for which we provide a probabilistic interpretation. We extend the construction to infinite graphs, exhibiting the analogs of the classical wired and free distributions on spanning forests. We give a sufficient geometric condition on the local spectral gap for the existence of a Poincaré inequality as well as the uniqueness of the infinite volume measure, and the exponential decay of correlations. We show that on any recurrent graph, the wired and free DLSF coincide. We construct examples where they do not, for example, unlike in the classical case, on $\mathbb Z^d$ for $d\geq 3$.

papers.title: A temporal graph dissimilarity measure capturing epidemic spreading behavior
papers.abstract: Comparing temporal networks is a challenging problem in network analysis. Commonly adopted methods compare structural properties of temporal graphs and can be highly sensitive to the pre-selected features. However, temporal networks are the support of dynamical processes, and a process may take place in statistically indistinguishable ways on structurally different temporal graphs. In particular, a dissimilarity measure that compares temporal graphs based on how spreading processes unfold on them is highly desirable. In this work, we first define the Time-Shift DTW, a dissimilarity between epidemic curves that accounts for both differences in their shape and temporal shifts. We then introduce Epidemic-Aware Temporal Graph Dissimilarity (EATGD), a deterministic and differentiable dissimilarity between temporal graphs that combines an embedding-based temporal graph distance with a set of topological and temporal features. Its parameters are calibrated using stochastic SIR simulations to maximize the correlation with the Time-Shift DTW, after which graph comparisons require no further epidemic simulations. Using empirical human proximity networks from the SocioPatterns collaboration and synthetic temporal graphs, we show that EATGD captures epidemic-based graph dissimilarity and generalizes across heterogeneous network settings. Its differentiability and computational efficiency make EATGD suitable for integration into machine-learning pipelines and provide a potential loss function for training generative models to reproduce epidemic dynamics without requiring an exact reconstruction of fine-grained network structure.

papers.title: Hölder regularity of the top Lyapunov exponent for random matrix products with low-dimensional equator
papers.abstract: We investigate the regularity of Lyapunov exponents for products of random invertible matrices of arbitrary dimension $d\ge 2$. We prove that the top Lyapunov exponent is pointwise Hölder continuous with respect to the Wasserstein-Hausdorff distance in the space of probability measures with compact support, in the case where this exponent is simple and the equator has dimension equal to or less than one.

papers.title: A Deterministic $0.401$-Approximation for Non-monotone Submodular Maximization under Matroid Constraints
papers.abstract: Submodular maximization arises in a wide range of combinatorial optimization problems and has been extensively studied from the perspective of approximation algorithms. For maximizing nonnegative, non-monotone submodular functions subject to a matroid constraint, randomized algorithms achieve a $0.401$-approximation, whereas obtaining comparable deterministic guarantees remains challenging. In this paper, we present a deterministic $0.401$-approximation algorithm in the exact value and independence oracle model, improving upon the previous deterministic guarantee of $(0.385-\varepsilon)$ \cite{ChenGLSZ2026}. Our algorithm builds on the extended multilinear extension and provides a deterministic implementation of the recursive guided framework underlying the randomized $0.401$-approximation algorithm. The main technical ingredient is a direction oracle supported on at most two partitioned matroid bases. This oracle simultaneously satisfies the growth condition required by the extended-multilinear update and an approximate stationarity condition needed to construct the recursive guides. The resulting finite-support representation enables exact evaluation of the relevant expectations and marginal values without random sampling. The algorithm uses polynomially many value- and independence-oracle queries.

papers.title: Construction of Regular Fat Linear Sets and Non-Representable q-Matroids
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be a prime power. An $(r, i)$-regular fat $\mathbb F_q$-linear set has exactly $r$ points of weight $i\ge2$, called fat points. All of its remaining points have weight one, and at least one such point occurs. We solve two open problems posed by three of the authors of this paper. First, we derive divisibility constraints on the point weights using the scalar stabilizer of the defining subspace. Consequently, a regular fat linear set of rank $2i$ in $\operatorname {PG}(1,q^n)$ has at most two or exactly $q + 1$ fat points. In the latter case, the fat points form an $\mathbb F_q$-subline. Second, we construct higher-dimensional regular fat linear sets whose fat points do not form an $\mathbb F_q$-subgeometry. In particular, for every $k\geq 3$ we obtain examples of rank $2k$ whose fat locus consists of an $\mathbb F_q$-subgeometry $\operatorname {PG}(k-2,q)$ in $\operatorname {PG}(k-1,q^4)$ together with one external point. This construction is then generalized further. Finally, we apply our projective-line results to $q$-matroid representability and present an infinite family of non-representable rank-two $q$-matroids arising from partial spreads.

papers.title: Chow polynomials and chain polynomials of matroids are not log-concave
papers.abstract: The Hilbert--Poincaré series of the Chow rings of the toric varieties of matroids, often called the \emph{Chow polynomials}, and the $f$-polynomial of their boundary complexes, called the \emph{chain polynomials}, have been conjectured to only have real zeros. We construct several explicit infinite families of matroids from finite geometries, whose multichain counts fail to be log-concave. They share a common geometric construction called \emph{hyperplane coalescence}, together with several classical operations in projective geometry and combinatorial designs. This induces failures of log-concavity for Chow, augmented Chow, chain, and $h$-polynomials of several explicit infinite families of matroids, disproving the real-rootedness conjectures of Ferroni--Schröter, Huh--Stevens, and Athanasiadis--Kalampogia-Evangelinou from the lowest possible ranks. As an application of the same mechanism, we also give counterexamples to the log-concavity of $h$-polynomials of graph associahedra, answering in the negative a question of Sack.

papers.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
papers.abstract: We show that matroid Stanley-Reisner rings can have essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, even at corank three. For every $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid with $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order deformation classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. These classes define a joint flat family whose $(m-1)$-jet has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, every nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and this quotient has an explicit module presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators. The construction is based on a computation of the full multigraded second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and its primary cup image in terms of flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. This computation also proves that $T^2$ vanishes precisely when every connected component has corank at most two, equivalently when the matroid has no $U_{1,4}$-minor, settling the conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello. The same criterion characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor.

papers.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
papers.abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $σ: \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $Λ$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in Λ} \|σ_i -σ_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $σ_{|\partial Λ}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main Hölder regularity statement in a large domain $Λ\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $σ$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the Hölder regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $σ\in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial Λ}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.

papers.title: Sustainable trees
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a connected graph and let $λ_1(X)$ denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. An edge $e$ of $X$ is sustainable if it can be deleted and replaced by a non-edge so that the resulting graph is connected and its spectral radius does not decrease; $X$ is sustainable if every edge is. We study this edgewise notion of spectral robustness for trees, where each replacement is an elementary exchange between trees on the same vertex set. We establish basic properties of sustainability and exhibit infinite families of sustainable and non-sustainable trees. Our main results concern trees with a vertex of large degree: if $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices with $Δ(T)\geq n/2$, then every vertex of maximum degree is a principal vertex, that is, a vertex at which the Perron vector is maximal. Building on this, we prove that every tree with $Δ(T)\geq n/2+1$ is non-sustainable, and we classify the sustainable trees in the boundary case $Δ(T)=n/2$: for $n\geq 4$, the only such trees are the double broom $B(2,n/2,n/2-1)$ and one exceptional tree on eight vertices. We conclude with open problems on the generalized tree-shift order and the asymptotic proportion of sustainable trees.

papers.title: Graph Distortion Distances, Gromov-Hausdorff and the Hardness of Gromov-Wasserstein
papers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of graph distortion distances, a family of graph metrics measuring how vertex distances differ between two graphs. Formally, these distances are defined in terms of standard matrix norms on the difference of distance matrices under an optimal vertex alignment. The resulting metrics have natural interpretations, corresponding to three ways of measuring the distortion of shortest-path distances: the maximum distortion among all vertex pairs (entrywise maximum norm), global aggregation (entrywise $p$-norms), and local aggregation (operator $p$-norms) of distortions. For maximum distortion, we show that approximation below a factor of two is NP-hard even for highly restricted trees. Due to the close connection to the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, we obtain a similar hardness result for the latter. In both cases, we show essentially optimal additive inapproximability. On the algorithmic side, we give a subcubic-time algorithm for optimal embeddings of connected graphs into paths, based on a structural decomposition along a diametral path. Additionally, we give a simple approximation algorithm when one input graph has a "relatively path-like" metric structure, i.e. has bounded pathlength. For local and global distortion, we derive various hardness results even for restricted inputs. Making use of a close connection between the global distortion distances and Gromov-Wasserstein distances, we give the first formal proof of NP-hardness of the latter, which has been claimed in the literature many times but has, to the best of our knowledge, never been correctly proven.

papers.title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
papers.abstract: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fréchet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.

papers.title: Optimal detection of geometry in random graphs and kernel matrices at critical thresholds
papers.abstract: Detection of geometry in random graphs and matrices has been extensively studied in recent years. For testing a dense random geometric graph on $n$ vertices with latent points in dimension $d$ against an Erdős--Rényi graph, the detection threshold $d\asymp n^3$ is well known since Bubeck, Ding, Eldan, and Rácz (2016). We sharpen this result by establishing the optimal asymptotic testing error in the critical regime $d/n^3\toλ\in(0,\infty)$. The log-likelihood ratio is shown to be asymptotically normal and dominated by the signed triangle count. Moreover, we consider testing the rank statistics of inner products between latent points against uniformly random ranks. We show that ranks preserve all asymptotic testing information available in the full matrix models, and a cubic statistic based on rank statistics attains the optimal asymptotic error. This then yields an asymptotically optimal test for random kernel matrices with a possibly unknown, strictly monotone kernel. The proofs combine the classical framework of Davies (1985) and Le Cam and Yang (1988) for asymptotic normality under information loss with conditional limit theorems for the models in consideration.

papers.title: K_1 of matroids
papers.abstract: Using the geometric realization spectral sequence and the Serre spectral sequence, we compute $K_1(\operatorname{Mat}_*)$, the first K-theory group of the proto-exact category of pointed matroids, answering a question of Jun, Sistko and Wright.

papers.title: Bipartite edge frustration of nut graphs: proofs and constructions
papers.abstract: The bipartite edge frustration of a graph $G$, $\varphi(G)$, is the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that is bipartite. Core graphs are singular graphs on $2$ or more vertices, for which the kernel of the adjacency matrix contains a full eigenvector. A nut graph is a core graph of nullity one. Nut graphs $G$ are non-bipartite. It is proved here that $\varphi(G) \geq 2$ if $G$ is a nut graph, i.e. every nut graph requires deletion of at least two edges to produce a bipartite graph. In addition, we give a constructive proof that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many chemical nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Furthermore, for $3 \leq d \leq 8$, the values $k$, for which a $d$-regular nut graph $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$ exists, are characterised. It is shown here that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many cubic polyhedral nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Two ways of producing larger nut graphs from smaller are described: the cut and frustration constructions. One straightforward consequence is that total double subdivision of a nut graph (i.e. simultaneous insertion of two degree-$2$ vertices into every edge) yields a nut graph.

papers.title: A sharp bound for the least signless Laplacian eigenvalue of triangle-free graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite simple triangle-free graph $G$ on $n\geq1$ vertices satisfies $q_{\min}(G)\leq7n/50$, where $q_{\min}(G)$ is the least eigenvalue of its signless Laplacian matrix $Q_G=D_G+A_G$, with $D_G$ the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A_G$ the adjacency matrix. The constant is sharp, since the Higman--Sims graph and its balanced blow-ups attain equality, as shown by de Lima, Nikiforov and Oliveira (2016). This proves the bound conjectured by Balogh, Clemen, Lidický, Norin and Volec (2023). The proof uses five test column vectors associated with an ordered edge to obtain a matrix Rayleigh inequality. Our use of local Rayleigh inequalities together with flag-algebra semidefinite programming is inspired by Zhou (2026). We use semidefinite programming and rational approximation to find the required positive semidefinite matrices, and complete the proof by exact correction and verification.

papers.title: Last-Coverage Probabilities of Random Walks on Cycle Graphs for Symmetric, Biased, and Time-Dependent Walks
papers.abstract: This paper studies the last-coverage vertex of a nearest-neighbour random walk on a cycle: the vertex most likely to be the final one discovered. We show that the visited vertices always form a single contiguous arc of the ring, a property we call the Connected Arc Property. This lets the walk be replaced by a two-state time-inhomogeneous Markov chain, which we call the interval-expansion representation, in which each expansion step has a probability given by the classical gambler's ruin formula. Within this framework we prove that the last-coverage probability of node k in an n-node cycle is (1-r)r^(n-1-k)/(1-r^(n-1)), where r = (1-p)/p and p is the clockwise transition probability. As p approaches 1/2, we recover the uniform distribution, giving an independent derivation of a classical result. For a walk with a deterministic time-varying bias, we give an exact series representation for the last-coverage probabilities, together with a finite truncation that serves as a computable, error-bounded approximation. All results are validated by Monte Carlo simulation, and we run experiments on sinusoidal time-varying bias. Finally, we compare generalized Petersen graphs with Erdos-Renyi graphs of matching size, finding that structural symmetry is associated with more uniform last-coverage distributions.

papers.title: Upper tail large deviation for the first passage time in the frog model on $Z^d$ with $d\geq 2$
papers.abstract: We study upper tail large deviations for the first passage time in the frog model on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge 2$. Let $\mathrm{T}(0,x)$ denote the first time at which the infection, started from the origin, reaches $x$, and let $μ$ be the associated time constant. We prove that, for any Euclidean unit vector $v\in\mathbb R^d$ and $ξ>0$, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} -\frac{1}{\mathfrak{s}_d(n)} \log \mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{T}(0,\lfloor nv\rfloor) \ge (μ(v)+ξ)n\bigr) =\mathfrak{r}_dξ, \] where $\mathfrak s_2(n)=n/\log n$ and $\mathfrak r_2=π$ for $d=2$; $\mathfrak s_d(n)=n$ and $\mathfrak r_d$ is the escape probability of simple random walk for $d\ge3$. Moreover, on the upper tail large deviation event, we show that a certain slowdown mechanism occurs near the endpoint. To rule out other mechanisms, we analyze the growth of the infection near the starting point using a modified exploration process, and investigate its propagation through the intermediate region using the renormalization and covering arguments.

papers.title: Quantitative Stability and Sample Complexity for Regularized Gromov-Wasserstein Distance
papers.abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance provides a principled framework for comparing two probability distributions supported on different metric spaces by matching their individual intrinsic geometric structures. In practice, the GW distance is estimated from finite samples and often incorporates regularization for statistical and computational tractability. This motivates a quantitative understanding of the stability and estimation error of regularized GW distances. In this work, we study a general family of divergence regularized GW distances, including entropy and Tsallis regularizations over the full range of powers, from a nonasymptotic perspective. Specifically, we establish Lipschitz continuity of the value of regularized GW and H{ö}lder continuity of its optimal coupling under Wasserstein perturbations of the input probability measures. Moreover, we derive the parametric rate of convergence for the empirical regularized (2,2)-GW distance on compactly supported Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: Poisson contingency tables, Gibbs permutations, and entropic optimal transport
papers.abstract: We study random contingency tables obtained by conditioning a matrix of independent Poisson entries on its row and column sums. We identify such a table with the block counts of a random permutation drawn from a Gibbs measure of Mallows type, an exact coupling whose normalizing constants recover Barvinok's permanent identity. We use this correspondence to study the table at three scales. For finite dimensions, a transference principle compares the table with a matrix of independent Poisson entries whose means form the static Schrödinger bridge, the solution of a discrete entropic optimal transport problem. As the dimensions grow and the margins and prior means converge, the normalized histogram of the table converges to a limiting Schrödinger bridge at a quantitative rate. The fluctuations of the table around the bridge are characterized in two complementary ways. Linear statistics satisfy a central limit theorem for bounded test functions, with limiting variance equal to the squared $L^2$-distance, under the bridge, of the test function to the subspace of additively separable functions; as a process they converge to white noise with intensity given by the bridge, conditioned to have vanishing marginals. Spectrally, the limiting spectral distribution of the centered table is governed by a Dyson equation whose variance profile is the density of the bridge. The key ingredient is an asymptotic formula for the partition function of the Gibbs measure in terms of a Fredholm determinant given by the canonical correlations of the bridge. For Mallows-type random permutations, our results prove Pal's conjecture on the limiting partition function and Mukherjee's conjecture on the central limit theorem for linear statistics, both in greater generality.

papers.title: Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs
papers.abstract: In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls. In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes. More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\toλ\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(λ)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity. For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.

papers.title: Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection: Statistical Properties and Distributionally Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: We study Markowitz's mean-variance portfolio optimization problem. When practically using this model, the mean vector and the covariance matrix of the assets returns often need to be estimated from the sample data. The sample errors will be propagated to the optimization output. In this paper, we consider three commonly used mean-variance models and build the asymptotic properties for the conventional sample approximations that are widely adopted and studied, by leveraging the stochastic optimization theory. We show that for all three models, under certain conditions the sample approximations have the desired consistency and achieve a convergence rate of square root of sample size, and the asymptotic variance depends on the first four moments of the returns. To address the variability and the uncertainty in the data driven portfolio optimization, we further consider the distributionally robust optimization (DRO) for the mean-variance model. For the ambiguity sets constructed by the $φ$-divergence and the Wasserstein distance, we build the tractable reformulations for the DRO models. We conduct numerical experiments to test the asymptotic properties for the estimation. We also conduct experiments to illustrate that the asymptotic normality might not hold when the fourth moments of the returns do not exist.

papers.title: Recurrent Barycenter Encoder: Prediction, Simulation and Applications to Time Series Analysis
papers.abstract: This dissertation has two parts. In the first part we theoretically develop a framework that extends the optimal transport barycenter problem from independent data with observed covariates to processes whose relevant covariate is their own history. Given a stationary stochastic process, our framework shows there exists an invertible transport map that extracts from it an iid component whose distribution is the barycenter of the conditional distributions of the input process on its own past. This extracted iid sequence thus captures the innovation or noise component of the process that is not explained by the process's own past. In the second part of this thesis we implement an effective algorithm to solve this problem and test it against synthetic data generated with some well-known models in time series analysis for which the solution is known in closed-form. We then show how this method can be applied to build a predictive sampler for such processes, and assess the accuracy of this predictive sampler both with the aforementioned synthetic data and with real-world time series such as the S&P 500 and Bitcoin 4-hour returns, and the daily records of the North Atlantic Oscillation index from the NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory. Finally, we demonstrate an application of the sampler to path simulation with a well-known time series model.

papers.title: Penalizations of Two-Dimensional Simple Random Walk by Direction-Dependent Excursion Counts and Edge-Crossing Counts
papers.abstract: We study penalizations of the two-dimensional simple random walk by functions of direction-dependent excursion counts and edge-crossing counts. The former record completed excursions with prescribed pairs of departure and return directions at the origin, whereas the latter record crossings of a prescribed set of unoriented edges incident to the origin. We determine the distributions of their almost surely finite terminal values and derive explicit path decomposition formulas involving the random walk conditioned to avoid the origin. Moreover, both families of penalized measures can be represented by weighting and normalizing the same universal $σ$-finite measure associated with local-time penalization at the origin. Thus, direction-dependent excursion counts, edge-crossing counts, and local time at the origin give rise to penalizations belonging to a common universality class.

papers.title: Variance Bounds for Minimum Perfect Matching Problem by Random Walk on Multinomial Distribution
papers.abstract: We establish variance upper bounds for the minimum perfect matching problem in general metric spaces under a geometric partition condition. As a principal application, let $H_n$ be the minimum perfect matching cost of $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, where $n$ is even and $d\ge2$. We prove $$\operatorname{Var}(H_n)\le C d n^{1-2/d},$$ where $C$ is independent of $n$ and $d$. This removes the logarithmic losses in earlier upper bounds in every dimension (Talagrand, 1995); in particular, the variance remains bounded in dimension two, answering an open question (Rhee, 1994). The proof relies on constructing a rapidly mixing Markov process with a multinomial stationary distribution.

papers.title: A Network Simplex Framework For Discrete Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: The network simplex method is a classical algorithm for minimum cost flow problems formulated as linear programs, that has attracted recent interest from the optimal transport community. Indeed, discrete optimal transport is a subclass of minimum cost flow for which network simplex techniques compute exact solutions while leveraging the inherent problem sparsity. However, extending these approaches to other, nonlinear optimal transport formulations has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this paper, we adapt the network simplex algorithm to unbalanced optimal transport. Our proposed framework is applicable to various unbalanced formulations, and can be implemented explicitly in the most common cases, including semi-unbalanced optimal transport. The resulting algorithms are memory-efficient, and perform competitively with existing approaches, as shown by our experiments on a range of transport and barycenter calculations.

papers.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous--Broder Theorem
papers.abstract: Random spanning forests provide probability models for partitions and Monte Carlo methods on graphs. In these applications, the distribution produced by a sampler determines which forest functionals can be estimated. The Aldous--Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but a direct calculation requires summing over all orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered. We evaluate this sum through an identity for rooted forests and real matrices with zero row sums. Under a nonsingularity condition on the principal submatrices encountered during growth, the sum of products of harmonic extension entries equals a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots. With one root, the sum is one. The identity gives a direct proof of the extended Aldous--Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state, without assuming reversibility or bidirectional transition support. It also gives the conditional distribution of the discovery order and the law of the forest obtained by stopping after all nonroot vertices have been visited. A completion weight describes the difference between this stopped-walk law and the weight-proportional forest law, including the support restriction needed for importance correction. Numerical examples illustrate the sampling implications. The identity, the Aldous--Broder theorem, and the stopped-forest law are formalized in Lean4.

papers.title: Interacting Stochastic Systems with Agent-Based Sampling and Connection-Based Reinforcement
papers.abstract: We introduce a general class of interacting reinforced stochastic systems evolving on a network. The dynamics are governed by two distinct interaction structures: a sampling network, which determines how information is acquired, and a reinforcement network, which determines how the sampled information influences future evolution. Processes generate Bernoulli observations through preferential, de-preferential, or mixed sampling, while observations are transmitted through an edge-dependent affine reinforcement mechanism. We formulate the dynamics as a stochastic approximation scheme and study their asymptotic behaviour. We establish sufficient conditions for almost sure convergence to a deterministic limit and, when the sampling and reinforcement graphs coincide, derive graph-theoretic criteria involving odd cycles, mixed-sampling vertices, and subcritical reinforcement. Under additional structural assumptions, we establish almost sure convergence and partial synchronization in a random-limit regime. In the deterministic regime, we also prove a law of the iterated logarithm and a central limit theorem under suitable spectral and regularity conditions. Finally, we show how the framework encompasses interacting urn models with edge-dependent reinforcement, urns with memory, and random walks with memory.

papers.title: Markovian Random Words, a Gaussian Random Matrix Model and Beyond
papers.abstract: After centering and scaling, the length of the longest weakly increasing subsequence of a finite-state Markov random word converges to a Brownian last-passage functional with dependent components. We investigate when this functional, and more generally the limiting RSK Young-diagram shape, admits a Gaussian random-matrix representation. We introduce Hermitian Gaussian matrices with correlated diagonal entries and show that isotropy of the Brownian covariance on the trace-zero hyperplane yields such a representation. Within this natural class of Hermitian models with independent Gaussian off-diagonal entries, we prove a rigidity theorem showing that isotropy, together with equality of the off-diagonal variances, characterizes the conditional largest-eigenvalue representation. Explicit three-letter non-cyclic Markov chains demonstrate that this representation is not universal: the limiting Brownian functional may fail to have the law of the largest eigenvalue of any centered jointly Gaussian $3\times 3$ Hermitian matrix. Finally, we extend the random-matrix identification to chains with non-uniform stationary distributions and to countable state spaces.

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part~1: expectation under the uniform null
papers.abstract: We study the expectation of the discrete total variation statistic $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$ of counts $X_1,\dots,X_n$ over $n$ ordered bins with sample size $N$, under the uniform multinomial null. In the notation used throughout the series, a reference distribution $\mathbf r$ defines $d_{\mathbf r}(x)=\|x-N\mathbf r\|_V$; here $\mathbf r=\mathbf u$ is uniform and we write simply $d$. We obtain an exact single-sum formula, a closed form in central trinomial coefficients valid for every $n\ge2$, with one-term evaluations at $n=2,4$ and a complete D-finite characterization for $n=3$. The per-edge expectation $W_N=E|X_2-X_1|$ satisfies an exact three-term recurrence, from which we derive its complete $1/N$ expansion with the $n$-independent constant $E(d^\circ/\sqrt{Nn})\to 2/\sqrtπ$ for the cyclic statistic $d^\circ=d^\circ_{\mathbf u}$, independent of the number of bins; the complementary sparse regime (fixed $N$, $n\to\infty$) is treated in a separate paper. Conditioning on a two-bin total reduces each edge to a symmetric random walk; as the subsequent parts of the series will show, this method carries the analysis to non-uniform reference laws.

papers.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
papers.abstract: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-N,N]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain. Athreya and Járai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $N\to\infty$. They asked whether, when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the resulting avalanche of topplings is finite. Járai and Redig (2008) proved that the answer is yes for $d\geq 3$, using the transience of random walk. We prove, using a different method, that avalanches are also finite for $d=2$.

papers.title: Fluctuations of the quadratic matching cost on the flat torus: dimensions five and higher
papers.abstract: We prove a central limit theorem for the quadratic matching cost between the uniform measure and its empirical counterpart on the flat torus in dimensions $d\ge5$. Let $μ$ be Haar probability measure on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and let $μ_n$ be the empirical measure of $n$ independent samples from $μ$. Then $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{W_2^2(μ_n,μ)-\mathbb{E}W_2^2(μ_n,μ)} {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(μ_n,μ))}} &\Longrightarrow N(0,1),\\ c_dn^{-1-4/d} \le \operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(μ_n,μ)) &\le C_dn^{-1-4/d}, \end{aligned} $$ for positive constants $c_d,C_d$ depending only on $d$ and all sufficiently large $n$. The proof introduces a random-walk approach to matching fluctuations. We construct a random walk that jumps between neighboring cells of the optimal partition and use it to describe how the matching cost responds to changes in the sample. Estimates for this walk control the effect of replacing one sample point and the interaction between two replacements. These bounds yield the variance estimates and allow us to apply a martingale central limit theorem.
